metadata.title: Reproduction package for: Rising biocapacity, falling ecological capital: how aggregation conceals composition
metadata.description:
Reproduction package (dataset and code) supporting the manuscript of record at https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202611.0852.v1. The manuscript itself lives at Preprints.org; this record exists to satisfy the journal's research-data requirement and to make the analysis re-runnable.

Study. Biocapacity combines land area and productivity in an aggregate annual account. Using a conserved-area two-land model with delayed ecological regeneration and delayed demographic response, the paper shows that conversion can raise the modeled account while ecological-capital land declines, gives sharp static bounds on what independent area and quality observations can identify, and decomposes the account change into signed integrated contributions from conversion, maintenance and retirement, restoration, quality and fast yield.

Empirical component. National Footprint Accounts Edition 2026 values for 1961-2023 show world biocapacity rising 24.86% while biocapacity per person falls 52.71% and production footprint per person rises 16.73%, with cropland contributing +24.06 percentage points, built-up land +7.44, and forest -5.95 to the aggregate change. These are annual account changes, not physical-stock observations.

Contents. LaTeX sources and PDFs of the manuscript (40 pp) and Supplementary Information (31 pp); all figure files; the nine table fragments; three analysis scripts with pinned dependencies; the frozen NFA Edition 2026 workbook and OWID cropland-area and cereal-yield series; and 26 numerical output files. All three scripts were re-executed in a clean copy of this package and reproduced the deposited data files byte-for-byte (26/26).

Scope. Model parameters are representative rather than fitted, and the simulations are conditional illustrations, not forecasts. No field data were collected for this study.

Attribution. NFA inputs and NFA-derived outputs retain CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution to Lo et al. (2026); OWID series retain their upstream terms. No provider endorsement is implied. This package supersedes the files of the earlier ECOMOD v35 upload (Zenodo 22554480) as the reproducibility record for this line of work.
